messages:
maria: Heads up — around 19:13 UTC ArgoCD prune wave for app-of-apps kicked off and we saw a huge burst of API 429s from the control plane, plus a ton of PodTerminated timeouts. Noticing NetworkPolicy egress denies on the kube-apiserver side.
kevin: Ugh, saw alerts. grafana shows apiserver request lat spiking and then a flurry of argo-server retries. Any recent change to prune concurrency or appset size?
devops-jen: I pushed a tweak yesterday to app-of-apps that added ~120 subapps (helm charts) for the eu-west cluster split. Might've bumped the fanout too high.
maria: That aligns. Logs show ArgoCD started prune for ~110 apps at once with prune-wave-size defaulting to 20 but waves overlapping because some apps took >30s to finalize. Example from argocd-server logs: `time=\"2026-03-18T19:13:04Z\" level=warn msg=\"prune operation timeout\" app=team-recs namespace=infra`
patrick: Also saw many failed PVC deletions because CSI controller couldn't reach storage API — but those failed deletes retried and kept holding finalizers which kept subsequent prune work queued.
kevin: So chain reaction: large fanout -> API 429 -> CSI/Storage retries -> finalizers stick -> more prune attempts -> longer windows so waves overlap.
sre-bot: Incident created: INC-20260318-argocd-prune-surge. Severity: P2. Runbook link: https://internal/runbooks/argocd-prune-surge
devops-jen: Quick mitigation suggestion: pause the app-of-apps rollout, scale down argocd-repo-server and argocd-application-controller to 1 replica to stop new reconciles, then resume with a smaller fanout and staggered waves. Thoughts?
maria: I prefer not to scale to 1 since it might block other regions. Instead I'd like to change `--prune-wave-size` and `--concurrent-reconciles` first. Current controller flags: `--prune-wave-size=20 --concurrent-reconciles=16`. If we lower to `5` and concurrency to `4`, that should throttle the bursts.
kevin: Good. Also add a per-app annotation to `argocd.argoproj.io/sync-wave` so the biggest apps go later. We can patch the appset generator to include it.
devops-jen: I'll open a quick patch: `kubectl -n argocd patch deployment argocd-application-controller --patch '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"argocd-application-controller","args":["--prune-wave-size=5","--concurrent-reconciles=4"]}]}}}}'`
patrick: For longer-term: update our Terraform modules that generate app-of-apps to create smaller sub-app groups and add `spec.syncOptions: [\"PruneLast=true\"]` for storage-heavy apps so PVCs get deleted at the end.
maria: Good call. Also looks like a NetworkPolicy we recently applied in eu-west blocks egress from some controller pods to the cloud storage control plane on 443 when traffic is SNATed. That caused additional retries. I'll open an exception for the argocd and csi controller subnets.
ops-bot: Deploy queued: patch argocd-application-controller args -> scheduling rolling restart. CI job: job-9274.
kevin: After reducing prune wave and adding NP exception, we should also enable argocd `app.propagationPolicy: \"background\"` for non-critical apps so deletes aren't immediate.
devops-jen: Done with the controller arg change and NP exception applied. Watching metrics.
maria: Update: apiserver 429s dropping back to baseline, ArgoCD reconcile rate stable. PVC finalizer queue drained slowly, ~25 left.
patrick: Follow-ups: 1) TF module change to appset sharding 2) Add smoke test that simulates prune waves in staging 3) Increase kube-apiserver request-throttle backoff settings. I'll file tickets.
kevin: Also add an alert threshold for sustained ArgoCD reconcile concurrency > 50 for >2m.
sre-bot: INC-20260318-argocd-prune-surge updated: mitigated, moving to monitoring.
maria: Nice work. Reminder: avoid large one-shot app-of-apps updates during business hours. Tagging @oncall for visibility. :thumbsup:
